title: Multi-tenant B2B SaaS with SSO federation

organisation.name: Tallyline
organisation.summary: Tallyline sells contract management software to businesses. Each customer is a tenant whose users sign in through the customer's own identity provider over SAML; tenant data shares one database protected by row-level security, and documents sit in per-tenant storage encrypted with per-tenant keys. Customers integrate through a public API with OAuth scopes and receive webhooks. Background workers on Kubernetes convert documents, deliver webhooks and send contract text to an LLM summariser. Support agents can sign in as a customer user through an impersonation tool after a colleague approves.

application_security.summary: Script in a contract on the legacy editor page runs for other users of the tenant
Document conversion fetches embedded links, including internal addresses

api_security.summary: The export endpoint with the read:all scope returns other tenants' data
A tenant registers a webhook URL that points at internal services

identity_access.summary: An assertion from one tenant's IdP signs a user into another tenant with the same email domain
90-day API tokens with read:all sit in customers' integration tools

data_security.summary: The shared workers' role can read and decrypt every tenant's documents
Workers connect with a database role that bypasses row-level security

ai_llm_security.summary: A contract from a counterparty carries instructions the summariser follows
Summary jobs put several tenants' text into one prompt

cloud_security.summary: A fetch from the conversion worker reaches the metadata service and the workers' role
Any pod in the workers' namespace gets the workers' cloud role

zero_trust.summary: Support impersonation gives full user sessions in any tenant
The SSO service trusts any signed assertion with a verified domain

security_operations.summary: An impersonation session starts at 2 a.m. with a self-approved request
API response sizes for one client jump a hundredfold

container_kubernetes.summary: A malicious document escapes the conversion container to the node
The workers' service account can read every secret in its namespace

network_security.summary: Workers can reach any address, including internal services, when delivering webhooks
The tenant database port is reachable from the public subnet

reviewNotes: Intermediate: tenant isolation is strong at the edges (row-level security, per-tenant keys, scopes) and weak in the middle (shared workers, a domain-matching SSO rule, impersonation).
